data.description: Proposed Canadian federal AI regulation. Part of Bill C-27 (Digital Charter Implementation Act, 2022).
data.notes: Part of Bill C-27 (Digital Charter Implementation Act). Proposes regulation of AI systems in Canada. Includes high-impact AI system requirements: risk assessments, mitigation measures, transparency, record-keeping. Establishes the AI and Data Commissioner. Status as of 2026-11-03: Bill C-27 died on the Order Paper when the 44th Parliament was prorogued/dissolved in early 2025.

data.description: Mandates cybersecurity programs and incident reporting for designated critical-infrastructure operators across finance, energy, transport, and telecom sectors.
data.notes: Originally introduced in the 44th Parliament as Part 2 of Bill C-26 (which died on the Order Paper upon dissolution in early 2025); reintroduced in the 45th Parliament, 1st Session as Bill C-8 (An Act respecting cyber security, amending the Telecommunications Act and making consequential amendments to other Acts), which received Royal Assent on June 15, 2026 (S.C. 2026, c. 9). Status verified as of 2026-11-03.

match_nodes.description: Bill C-34 — Safe Social Media Act (Digital Safety Act)

data.official_name: An Act to enact the Digital Safety Act and the Digital Safety Commission of Canada Act and to make consequential and related amendments to other Acts
alternate_names: Digital Safety Commission of Canada Act
data.description: Proposed Canadian federal legislation regulating social media platforms and AI chatbot services accessible to Canadians, with a statutory Duty to Act Responsibly toward child users and mandatory safeguards against manipulative AI companion design.
data.notes: Status: Proposed (45th Parliament, 1st Session; First Reading June 10, 2026; verified as of 2026-11-03). Explicitly brings interactive AI chatbot services within the scope of the Digital Safety Act: prohibits bots from deceptively claiming to be human or impersonating licensed medical/mental health professionals, bars design features intended to induce emotional dependency or harm in minors, requires risk assessments and mitigation plans, and establishes the Digital Safety Commission of Canada.

match_nodes.description: National Security Act, 2017 (S.C. 2019, c. 13 / Bill C-59)

data.official_name: An Act respecting national security matters (National Security Act, 2017)
alternate_names: Loi de 2017 sur la sécurité nationale
data.description: Enacted Canadian federal statute overhauling Canada's national security accountability, intelligence oversight, cyber security mandate (Communications Security Establishment Act), and statutory parliamentary review processes.
data.notes: Status: In force (Royal Assent June 21, 2019; S.C. 2019, c. 13; verified as of 2026-11-03). Enacted the National Security and Intelligence Review Agency Act (Part 1) and the Communications Security Establishment Act (Part 3), and established a mandatory comprehensive parliamentary review of the Act's provisions starting in its fourth year (Section 168(1)).

match_nodes.description: National Security and Intelligence Review Agency Act (S.C. 2019, c. 13, s. 2)

data.official_name: National Security and Intelligence Review Agency Act
alternate_names: Loi sur l'Office de surveillance des activités en matière de sécurité nationale et de renseignement
data.description: Federal statute establishing the National Security and Intelligence Review Agency (NSIRA) with cross-government authority to review any federal department or agency's national security or intelligence activities.
data.notes: Status: In force (enacted via Part 1, s. 2 of the National Security Act, 2017, S.C. 2019, c. 13; Justice Laws chapter N-16.62; verified as of 2026-11-03). Requires annual public reports to the Prime Minister tabled in Parliament and statutory annual reviews of CSIS and CSE activities.

match_nodes.description: National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians Act (S.C. 2017, c. 15)

data.official_name: National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians Act
alternate_names: Loi sur le Comité des parlementaires sur la sécurité nationale et le renseignement
data.description: Federal statute establishing the cross-party National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians (NSICOP) to review the legislative, regulatory, policy, administrative, and financial framework for national security and intelligence in Canada.
data.notes: Status: In force (Royal Assent June 22, 2017; S.C. 2017, c. 15; verified as of 2026-11-03). Section 8 empowers NSICOP to review the overarching legislative, regulatory, and strategic policy framework for national security and intelligence; Section 21 requires annual and special reports to be tabled in Parliament; Section 34 mandates a comprehensive five-year statutory parliamentary review.
